prose_updates.tldr: For every rationally identifiable acyclic linear Gaussian mixed graph, eliminating the supported disturbance covariances first leaves missing-bidirected cubic equations in \(n(n+1)/2+|D|\) variables and gives the graph-sensitive bound \(ID_G\leq\mathfrak B(G)=\lfloor2(15/2)^{2^{n(n+1)/2+|D|-1}}\rfloor\). Structural coefficients have direct certificates at this cutoff, and all disturbance coordinates follow by recursive degree-three certificates. This yields a graph-sensitive total exact call to the degree-bounded identification algorithm. For directed indegree at most two, \(|D|\leq2n-3\) sharpens the graph-independent cutoff to \(U_2(1)=15\) and \(U_2(n)=\lfloor2(15/2)^{2^{n(n+1)/2+2n-4}}\rfloor\) for \(n\geq2\). The exact value of \(ID_{K_6}\) and the bounded-versus-unbounded elbow for \(D_2(n)\) remain open.

project_justification.gap: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma's formula-producing algorithm requires a supplied degree cutoff. Their subclass bounds are \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) for half-trek and instrumental cutsets and \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\) for auxiliary cutsets. The graph-sensitive effective cutoff proved here makes the full rationally identifiable acyclic search total, and its indegree-two corollary supplies a graph-independent schedule. No result yet decides whether the sharp frontier \(D_2(n)\) is bounded uniformly in \(n\), nor its least constant or growth rate.
project_justification.fill: The note eliminates supported disturbance coordinates from the cubic covariance graph ideal, applies the published Dubé bound in only \(n(n+1)/2+|D|\) variables, and proves the lexicographic extraction of direct structural certificates. The disturbance coordinates are recovered afterward by denominator-one degree-three recursive certificates. This compiles into a graph-sensitive unconditional total formula-returning schedule and, using \(|D|\leq2n-3\), a sharper graph-independent indegree-two schedule. It also proves \(ID_{K_6}\leq7\) by cancelling two central-seed quadratics. The exact \(K_6\) degree and the sharp bounded-versus-unbounded frontier remain explicit certified-computation and structural-algebra questions; the disproved windmills are not used as a lower family.

prose_updates.related_work: Hollering, Misra, and Sturma define \(ID_G\), return minimum-degree rational formulas below a prespecified cutoff, and give the half-trek and instrumental-cutset bounds \(2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}+1\) and the auxiliary-cutset bound \(s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^4+2s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^3+s_{\mathrm{HMS}}^2\). Dubé's general Gröbner-basis theorem supplies the published degree bound used after the new Omega-first elimination step; the structural elimination identity, lexicographic certificate extraction, degree-three disturbance recovery, and schedule compilation are proved in this note. Foygel, Draisma, and Drton provide the half-trek baseline, and Kumor, Chen, and Bareinboim and Kumor, Cinelli, and Bareinboim provide the two cutset criteria. Van der Zander et al., Gupta and Bläser, and Briefs and Bläser develop tree and missing-cycle mechanisms adjacent to the \(K_6\) calculation, but they do not determine its source-defined recursive degree. Dörfler et al. give a total generic-identification decision benchmark without the same rational formula output. Mareis, Sturma, and Drton remain adjacent fixed-estimator inference work: the regular-chart delta-method and simultaneous Wald theorem applies to any fixed deterministic rational map and is logically independent of either stopping cutoff.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The cutoffs \(\mathfrak B(G)=\lfloor2(15/2)^{2^{n(n+1)/2+|D|-1}}\rfloor\) and its indegree-two envelope \(U_2(n)\) are effective elimination bounds, not sharp estimates of \(ID_G\) or \(D_2(n)\). The Omega-first proof guarantees direct covariance-only formulas at that degree for structural coefficients; disturbance coordinates are instead recovered recursively after the structural stage by degree-three certificates. The proof \(ID_{K_6}\leq7\) supplies no lower bound, no auxiliary-cutset failure result, and no substitute for the required exact filtered-closure artifact. The former two-parent windmills are generically infinite-to-one and cannot support a lower bound on the rationally identifiable class. No replacement dimension-feasible birational family or theorem deciding whether \(\sup_nD_2(n)\) is finite has been established.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The established structural results are the recursive closure characterization, the exact values \(D_2(1)=1\), \(D_2(2)=2\), and \(D_2(3)=3\), the graph-sensitive inequality \(ID_G\leq\mathfrak B(G)\) for every rationally identifiable acyclic mixed graph, its sharper indegree-two envelope \(D_2(n)\leq U_2(n)\), the corresponding graph-sensitive and graph-independent total exact stopping schedules, and the upper bound \(ID_{K_6}\leq7\). The exact value of \(ID_{K_6}\), any claim that \(K_6\) lies outside auxiliary cutsets, the bounded-versus-unbounded elbow, and a matching lower family remain open. The old padded windmills are expressly excluded from the identifiable class. The fixed-dimensional regular-chart inference theorem remains independent of how a deterministic rational map was selected or computed. No semiparametric efficiency, adaptive-selection validity, growing-dimensional Gaussian approximation, singular-chart coverage, or cutoff sharpness is claimed.

statement_notes.justification: Eliminating supported disturbance coordinates gives a graph-sensitive structural cutoff, and the indegree-two edge count converts it into a sharper unconditional graph-uniform bound.
statement_notes.gap: The elimination cutoffs are not asserted to be sharp; direct cutoff-degree certificates are proved for structural coordinates, while disturbance coordinates are recovered recursively at degree three.
statement_notes.consumer: Both the graph-sensitive and graph-independent exact stopping schedules use this bound.

statement_notes.justification: The graph-sensitive elimination theorem converts the formula search into an unconditional total procedure at a computable input-specific cutoff, with a sharper graph-independent indegree-two alternative.
statement_notes.gap: Existing formula-producing computation requires a cutoff, while the effective cutoffs supplied here are not claimed to equal the intrinsic sharp frontier.
statement_notes.consumer: Users obtain auditable graph-sensitive or graph-independent stopping rules, exact positive or negative certificates, and explicit worst-case arithmetic bounds.
